questions.stem: Which city serves as the permanent headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?

options.option_text: Geneva, Switzerland — home to WHO and ILO offices
Montreal, Canada — chosen as ICAO's seat in 1944
New York, USA — where the UN General Assembly meets
Vienna, Austria — seat of UNIDO and IAEA offices

questions.explanation: ICAO was established by the Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation (1944) and its permanent headquarters was set in Montreal, Canada. Geneva is the most tempting distractor as it hosts WHO, ILO, and WTO, but ICAO specifically is based in Montreal.

questions.stem: Which UN body was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 'for its efforts to combat hunger, for its contribution to bettering conditions for peace in conflict-affected areas, and for acting as a driving force in efforts to prevent the use of hunger as a weapon of war'?

options.option_text: UNICEF — UN Children's Fund focused on child nutrition
FAO — Food and Agriculture Organization, Rome-based
WFP — World Food Programme, headquartered in Rome
IFAD — International Fund for Agricultural Development

questions.explanation: The WFP (World Food Programme) won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020. FAO is the classic wrong answer — it is also Rome-based and food-focused, but FAO is a normative and standards-setting body, whereas WFP is the UN's operational emergency food-relief arm.

questions.stem: UNIDO (United Nations Industrial Development Organization), which promotes inclusive and sustainable industrial development, has its headquarters in which European city?

options.option_text: Geneva, Switzerland — major hub for WTO, WHO, and ILO
Vienna, Austria — also hosts IAEA and the CTBTO
Brussels, Belgium — seat of major EU institutions
Rome, Italy — home to FAO, WFP, and IFAD agencies

questions.explanation: UNIDO is headquartered in Vienna, Austria — making Vienna a triple UN-agency hub alongside IAEA and the CTBTO (Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization). Geneva hosts more UN bodies overall, but UNIDO specifically is in Vienna.

questions.stem: Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) — supplementary international reserve assets allocated to member countries to supplement official reserves — were created in 1969 by which institution?

options.option_text: World Bank Group, headquartered in Washington D.C.
Bank for International Settlements, based in Basel
International Monetary Fund (IMF), Washington D.C.
Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Beijing-based

questions.explanation: SDRs were created by the IMF in 1969 to supplement member countries' official reserves and ease balance-of-payments pressures. The World Bank is the most common wrong answer — it provides development finance, whereas the IMF focuses on monetary cooperation, exchange-rate stability, and liquidity support.

questions.stem: The UNHCR (UN Refugee Agency) was established by a UN General Assembly resolution in which year, initially as a temporary body with a three-year mandate?

options.option_text: 1945 — the same year the UN Charter came into force
1948 — year the Universal Declaration of HR was adopted
1950 — when UNGA Resolution 428(V) established UNHCR
1956 — triggered by mass displacement during the Hungarian crisis

questions.explanation: UNHCR was created by UNGA Resolution 428(V) on 14 December 1950, beginning operations on 1 January 1951. Option D (1956) is a shrewd distractor — the Hungarian refugee crisis was a landmark early test for UNHCR, but the agency already existed six years before that event.

questions.stem: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), one of the oldest surviving intergovernmental organizations and now a UN specialized agency, was founded in 1865 under what original name?

options.option_text: International Radiotelegraph Union, formed in Berlin, 1906
International Telegraph Union, established in Paris, 1865
Universal Postal Union, founded in Paris in the same year
League of Nations Telegraph Committee, Geneva, 1920

questions.explanation: The ITU was founded as the 'International Telegraph Union' in Paris on 17 May 1865, making it among the world's oldest intergovernmental organizations. It was renamed ITU at the 1932 Madrid Plenipotentiary Conference. Option C is a crafted trap — the UPU was founded in 1874 in Bern, not Paris in 1865.

questions.stem: Which UN specialized agency publishes the twice-yearly 'World Economic Outlook' — a flagship report providing global growth projections that finance ministries and central banks treat as a primary macroeconomic reference?

options.option_text: World Bank Group, which publishes World Development Report
UNCTAD, which releases the Trade and Development Report
International Monetary Fund (IMF), Washington D.C.
WTO Secretariat, which publishes the World Trade Report

questions.explanation: The IMF publishes the 'World Economic Outlook' twice a year (April and October), providing global GDP forecasts and fiscal policy analysis. The World Bank is the most common wrong answer — it publishes the 'World Development Report'. Distinguishing which body publishes which flagship report is a frequently tested nuance in banking and SSC exams.
